findings.title: Draining flag gives no drain window - listener closes microseconds later
findings.evidence: The comment says balancers should stop sending new traffic, but 'draining.Store(true)' is immediately followed by context.WithTimeout + srv.Shutdown(shutdownCtx), and Shutdown closes the listeners at once. Any LB still routing (health-check interval not yet elapsed) hits a closed listener and gets connection refused/502.
findings.recommendation: Insert a bounded drain delay between the flag flip and Shutdown (e.g. time.Sleep or a timer of the LB health-check period, ~2x poll interval), sized so drain delay + in-flight deadline still fits inside the orchestrator termination grace period, and count the delay inside the same overall deadline.

findings.title: Second signal cannot force early exit
findings.evidence: 'defer stop()' keeps the signal handler registered for the whole process lifetime; once ctx.Done fires, a subsequent SIGTERM/SIGINT is swallowed by NotifyContext and has no effect, so an operator cannot abort the up-to-15s drain.
findings.recommendation: Call stop() immediately after <-ctx.Done() returns (before Shutdown) so a second signal gets default behaviour (process kill), or install a second-signal handler that calls srv.Close() and exits non-zero.

findings.title: No test covers drain state or shutdown deadline
findings.evidence: The new file adds behavior -- 'var draining atomic.Bool' plus the 15s Shutdown/Close fallback -- with no test exercising the 503 health response after the flag flips or the deadline-expiry path.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that serves on an ephemeral listener, sends SIGTERM (or triggers the ctx.Done branch), asserts /healthz returns 503 while draining, asserts in-flight requests complete, and asserts the forced Close path fires when a handler exceeds the deadline.
